knownErrors.symptom: an @export NodePath like "/Main/Beacon" resolves to null via get_node_or_null() when called from a nested node, silently breaking gaze/follow/reference wiring with no error
knownErrors.rootCause: a leading-slash NodePath resolves from the actual SceneTree root (get_tree().root), not the edited scene's own root node - it needs the "/root/<SceneRootName>/..." prefix, not "/<SceneRootName>/..."
protection: always prefix absolute Godot NodePaths with /root/<SceneName>/
verify resolution with a game_eval read of the exported var immediately after wiring, not just visually

knownErrors.symptom: mouse-look makes the tracked subject appear to spin/swing across the screen instead of staying anchored while the world rotates around it
knownErrors.rootCause: mouse yaw/pitch was applied to a rig that only rotates in place at a fixed offset (first-person look), instead of a true orbit rig whose camera swings in an arc around the subject's origin
protection: orbit rigs must rotate at the tracked subject's own origin, with the camera offset behind/above and pre-tilted to face back at that origin
verify by checking the subject's screen-space position stays roughly constant while yaw/pitch change, not just that the view moves at all

knownErrors.symptom: an EditorPlugin or gate script fails to load at all (parse error), silently disabling every check it contains
knownErrors.rootCause: an `is SomeClassName` type check referenced a class that doesn't exist as a native Godot type or a registered class_name in the project
protection: use n.get_class() == "ClassName" (string compare) instead of `is ClassName` when a class's existence in the target project isn't guaranteed
smoke-test any new editor plugin actually enables without a parse error before relying on its gate

knownErrors.symptom: Cyrillic text, curly quotes, or em-dashes in an existing file turn into mojibake (e.g. Ра…-style garbage) and a stray BOM appears at the top, after a PowerShell install/patch script touches that file
knownErrors.rootCause: Windows PowerShell 5.1's Get-Content -Raw defaults to the system ANSI codepage when no -Encoding is given, misreading a BOM-less UTF-8 source file; the corrupted string is then re-saved via Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 (which also adds a BOM in 5.1), baking the corruption in
protection: always pass -Encoding UTF8 to both Get-Content -Raw and Set-Content when a PowerShell script reads-then-writes an existing text file
diff every file an installer touches for mojibake/BOM before committing, not just for the intended content change

knownErrors.symptom: a scene renders fine when launched via the MCP/editor Play button but shows a blank grey screen with no visible error when run as a real standalone .exe/window
knownErrors.rootCause: a `var x := expr` where expr's type can't be statically inferred (e.g. the builtin generic max()/min()/clamp() instead of maxi/mini/clampi/maxf/minf/clampf) is only a warning in the editor's live Play session, but the same project can have warnings-as-errors enabled for exported/standalone runs - the affected script (often an autoload or a node's own controller) fails to load entirely, so its Camera3D/logic never runs and the viewport shows nothing but the default clear color
protection: always give `var x := ...` an explicit type, or use the typed builtin variant (maxi/maxf/mini/minf/clampi/clampf), for any value assigned from a generic Variant-returning builtin

before calling a scene 'done', launch it via the real standalone executable (godot.exe --path <project>, not just the editor's embedded Play) and check its console/log for SCRIPT ERROR / Parse Error lines, not only a visual screenshot

knownErrors.symptom: moving the camera around a dark voxel scene doesn't visibly read as the world moving, because the hero terrain/mountain silhouette around the focal object (eye, character, etc.) blends into the near-black background instead of having a readable edge
knownErrors.rootCause: a 'dark' material was tuned by albedo/emission numbers alone (e.g. albedo #0b0a09 on a #020201 background) without checking rendered contrast, and roughness=1.0 gave it zero specular response, so no light source - however placed - could ever put a visible highlight on its edges; darkness in a cinematic void scene must still contain readable geometry, not just be technically non-zero brightness
protection: give hero-adjacent dark materials roughness < 1.0 (e.g. ~0.85) so a grazing rim/key light can actually put a specular highlight on their silhouette edges
add a dedicated rim/key DirectionalLight3D (or equivalent) angled to graze across hero terrain specifically for silhouette definition, separate from any fill light on the main subject
verify by screenshot, not by reading material property values - a material can be 'lit' in the editor properties panel and still be visually indistinguishable from the background at render time

knownErrors.symptom: AI presents a visual result as finished/ready/done while it's still clearly below the user's approved quality bar for that project
knownErrors.rootCause: no persistent, checked-every-time threshold table existed - visual completeness was judged by feel in the moment rather than against a fixed, user-set number per category
protection: data/reference-visual-gate.json holds a hard, user-set per-category threshold table per project - see DESKTOP_AI_INSTALL_AND_VERIFY.md's REFERENCE_VISUAL_GATE block
self-score every category from a fresh screenshot against the reference before using done/ready/final language; if any category is under threshold, report IN PROGRESS with the specific gap instead
the AI may not lower a threshold or skip the gate itself for any reason, including time or effort constraints - only the user can relax it

knownErrors.symptom: an orbit-style camera rig visibly orbits SOMETHING and looks correct in a single static screenshot, but a real mouse/yaw sweep sends the tracked subject drifting off-frame instead of staying centered
knownErrors.rootCause: the rig node's own scene-level `position` was set to the intended back/up camera offset (e.g. (0, 1.4, 13)), duplicating an offset the rig's script ALSO applies internally to its camera child in _ready() - so the actual orbit center ended up 13 units away from the tracked subject instead of at the subject's own origin
protection: the orbit rig's own position must be exactly (0,0,0), at the tracked subject's origin - the back/up offset belongs only on the rig's internally-built camera child, never duplicated on the rig node's own transform

verify with game_eval: the subject's global_position must be byte-identical before and after a real yaw change, not just 'the view moved' - see templates/godot-voxel-game-starter/orbit_camera_rig.gd for the canonical, verified-correct shape

knownErrors.symptom: a node created via the godot-ai MCP's node_create tool lands as a direct child of the scene root instead of the intended parent, with no error
knownErrors.rootCause: the tool's parent parameter is named `parent_path`, not `parent` - passing `parent` is accepted as an unrecognized-but-harmless extra field and silently ignored rather than rejected
protection: always pass `parent_path` (never `parent`) to node_create
after creating a node with a non-root intended parent, verify its actual path in the tool's own result before proceeding, rather than assuming the requested parent was honored

knownErrors.symptom: moving/flying the player-controlled subject drags the surrounding terrain/world geometry along with it instead of leaving it behind
knownErrors.rootCause: the world/terrain generator node was added as a CHILD of the hero node (often done for convenience, to get a 'hero embedded in the world' look for free at spawn) - any transform change on the hero then applies to the whole subtree including the world
protection: world/terrain and the hero are always siblings under a common static parent, never parent/child in either direction

to get an 'embedded at spawn' look, position the hero at the world object's socket coordinates instead of parenting - see godot-voxel-game-baseline.json's worldHeroSeparation rule and mountain_wall.gd / voxel_eye_runtime.gd in dark-void-scene for the fixed pattern
verify with game_eval: after moving the hero, the world object's global_position must be unchanged

knownErrors.symptom: a hero/character built from voxels reads as a flat sheet or an oversized blob pasted onto the world instead of a distinct, detailed subject
knownErrors.rootCause: the hero was built using the same voxel size and roughly the same overall scale as the surrounding world/terrain geometry, so nothing visually distinguishes 'the thing you play as' from 'the environment'
protection: standing rule (data/godot-voxel-game-baseline.json, heroVoxelToWorldVoxelRatio): hero voxels are always exactly 5x smaller than world voxels, both per-cube and in overall subject scale - const HERO_VOX := WORLD_VOX / 5.0
apply this from the start of every new Godot voxel project, not as a later fix

knownErrors.symptom: a three.js Object3D subclass's own local matrix gets NaN in its translation (elements 12-14) after scene.updateMatrixWorld() / renderer.render(), with everything appearing to construct correctly beforehand (position/rotation/quaternion all read as valid, non-NaN numbers) - camera/rig ends up nowhere, or the whole canvas stays blank/background-only
knownErrors.rootCause: isolated and reproduced in this repo's vendored three.js build (shared/vendor/three) plus this session's browser-automation test harness: an Object3D subclass instance with an own property literally named `pivot` (assigned a THREE.Object3D, even if never added to the scene tree) reproducibly triggers the corruption; renaming the property alone fixes it with everything else identical. The string is not present anywhere in the vendored three.js source, so the exact mechanism is unconfirmed (likely a harness/JIT-specific interaction, not a documented library bug) - but it is 100% reproducible and trivial to avoid
protection: never name an Object3D subclass's own instance property `pivot` in this codebase - use `pitchGroup` or similar instead, as shared/dark-void-scene-runtime.mjs's OrbitCameraRig does

if a scene renders blank/background-only despite no console errors, check camera.matrixWorld.elements for NaN (Number.isNaN, not just falsy/JSON-null) as a first diagnostic step, then binary-search which own property on which Object3D ancestor triggers it by renaming

knownErrors.symptom: browser refuses to load an ES module with "Expected a JavaScript-or-Wasm module script but the server responded with a MIME type of application/octet-stream"
knownErrors.rootCause: server.js's static-file mime table only mapped .js, not .mjs — every .mjs file served by the local dev server (server.js) fell through to the application/octet-stream default, which browsers refuse to execute as a module script
protection: server.js's mime table must include '.mjs': 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8' alongside '.js'
verify any new .mjs-based runtime with a live browser load (curl -I on the URL is not sufficient — confirm Content-Type AND that the module actually evaluates), not just a Node unit test
knownErrors.solution: add '.mjs': 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8' to server.js's mime map

knownErrors.symptom: test/multi-ai-peer-review.test.js fails with 'SyntaxError: Unterminated string in JSON' or an assertion that exit code is null instead of 0
knownErrors.rootCause: scripts/multi-ai-peer-review.cjs shells out to `git diff --name-only origin/master...<branch>` for up to 10 long-lived ai/*/opencode/* branches via spawnSync with no maxBuffer override (Node default ~1MB); the test's own spawnSync wrapping the whole script also had no override. As the repo accumulates more branches and diff volume, either call point silently truncates output mid-JSON once it crosses ~1MB, which can happen from unrelated commits on unrelated branches, not from the branch under test
protection: scripts/multi-ai-peer-review.cjs's run() helper must set a generous maxBuffer (64MB) on every spawnSync call
test/multi-ai-peer-review.test.js's runGate() must also set maxBuffer (32MB) on its own spawnSync wrapping the script
when this test fails, first reproduce it in an unrelated worktree/branch to rule out an environment-wide (branch-count/diff-volume) cause before assuming a regression in the branch under test
knownErrors.solution: add maxBuffer overrides to both the inner script spawnSync calls and the outer test spawnSync call

knownErrors.symptom: GitHub Actions CI fails at the very first `npm ci` step with `npm error code EUSAGE ... can only install packages when your package.json and package-lock.json ... are in sync`, blocking every check on every PR based on the affected branch
knownErrors.rootCause: a dependency (e.g. @mediapipe/tasks-vision, pngjs) was added to package.json without running `npm install` to regenerate package-lock.json and committing the result — npm ci (used in CI, unlike npm install used locally) refuses to proceed on a stale lock file
protection: whenever package.json dependencies/devDependencies change, run `npm install` and commit the resulting package-lock.json diff in the same change

if CI's npm ci step fails, check the error for 'Missing: <pkg>@<version> from lock file' before assuming a real test regression — it means the base branch itself has lockfile drift, unrelated to the PR's own changes
knownErrors.solution: run `npm install` to regenerate package-lock.json and commit it alongside the package.json change

knownErrors.symptom: a claimed Supabase database state (e.g. 'this migration is already applied') does not match what direct queries via the Supabase MCP tools show, or an MCP session cannot see a project the user references by name
knownErrors.rootCause: more than one Supabase project can share a similar or identical human-readable name (e.g. two projects both nameable as some variant of "Improve world"), and a given MCP/tool session may only have access to a subset of an organization's projects — trusting a project by display name alone, or assuming an MCP session sees every project, produces false conclusions about database state
protection: always confirm the exact project_id (ref), never just the display name, before running any migration or destructive query

if a claimed database state can't be reproduced via direct query, report the discrepancy honestly (what you see vs. what was claimed) and ask for the correct project_id rather than either blindly trusting the claim or unilaterally overriding it
a project MCP tools cannot see is not necessarily wrong or nonexistent — the user may have access this session does not

knownErrors.symptom: a migration that works in production fails at runtime (missing table/column) when applied to a preview/staging Supabase project, even though `create or replace function` itself succeeded with no error
knownErrors.rootCause: Postgres does not validate table/column references inside a plpgsql function body at CREATE FUNCTION time, only at first EXECUTE — so a migration file that only creates a function assuming certain base tables/columns already exist (e.g. 'using existing voxel_worlds + voxel_world_events') can be applied cleanly to an environment that lacks those prerequisites, deploying a function that is silently broken until first called. Preview/staging projects can have a materially different (often older, consolidated, or partially-provisioned) base schema than production, even when the migration file history in the repo looks linear
protection: before applying any migration to a non-production project, run a schema-compatibility check against the exact tables/columns/constraints the migration body references — do not infer compatibility from the migration file list or CREATE FUNCTION succeeding

list_migrations output on a target project can use a completely different naming/versioning scheme than the repo's local migration filenames (e.g. consolidated/squashed history) — do not assume version-number alignment implies schema alignment

if a migration assumes prerequisite schema (tables/columns) that the target project does not have, do not apply it — report the gap and let a human decide whether/how to backfill the prerequisite schema, since inventing new table/column/RLS design unilaterally is a real architectural decision

knownErrors.symptom: OpenHuman's ordinary chat UI reports knowing nothing about a project, even though agentmemory is healthy, OpenHuman's config correctly points at it, and a REST-level cross-memory roundtrip test (write a probe, search for it, find it) passes
knownErrors.rootCause: REST cross-memory PASS only proves agentmemory is reachable and can round-trip an arbitrary probe string — it does not prove the memory store contains real, substantive project knowledge. A connectivity smoke test (e.g. CHECK_COLLECTIVE_BRAIN.cmd's own 'Memory save/recall' probe) that writes a short random string and confirms it comes back can itself be the only thing populating a project's memory, crowding out (or simply being mistaken for) actual curated knowledge — this repo's own health check had been doing exactly that for days before anyone noticed the project's memory had no real facts in it
protection: treat "REST cross-memory roundtrip PASS" and "ordinary chat surfaces real knowledge PASS" as two distinct claims, never conflate them — a doctor/test reporting both separately (not just one combined status) is required

before diagnosing an ordinary-chat memory gap, actually list/search the target memory store's content for the project (not just probe for a freshly-written test string) — a project can have dozens of memory entries and still contain zero real facts

a connectivity health-check script that writes its own probe data into the same durable memory store it is checking will pollute that store over repeated runs — prefer a dedicated ephemeral/test namespace, or at minimum distinct low-relevance concepts, for pure connectivity probes so they do not compete with real knowledge in search ranking
knownErrors.solution: build a curated, hand-authored knowledge pack (not a raw dump) and write it into the real memory store via the existing remember() mechanism; verify via the same search path the chat UI itself uses

knownErrors.symptom: a launcher/script that starts OpenHuman.exe with a special env var (e.g. OPENHUMAN_ACTION_DIR) reports success (exit code 0) but no new window appears and the setting has no visible effect
knownErrors.rootCause: OpenHuman enforces a pre-CEF single-instance mutex (real log line: '[single-instance] pre-CEF mutex held by primary; secondary exiting (OPENHUMAN-TAURI-A fix)'). If ANY OpenHuman.exe is already running — including invisibly, with no taskbar entry the user notices — a second launch exits almost instantly, cleanly, having created no window and applied no env var to the already-running primary. There is no supported way to push a new action_dir into an already-running instance from outside it.
protection: before launching, check for an existing OpenHuman.exe process and tell the user explicitly if one is found, instead of launching into the trap and reporting a false success
never treat 'exit code 0' as proof a GUI actually appeared — check for a live process with a nonzero MainWindowHandle a few seconds after Start-Process

the real fix requires the existing instance to be fully closed first; CloseMainWindow() may not be enough (the app can ignore WM_CLOSE or minimize to tray) — Stop-Process may be needed as a second step
knownErrors.solution: scripts/openhuman-launch-check.js (OPENHUMAN_GUI_LAUNCH_CHECK) — distinguishes executableExists from guiLaunchVerified using a written launch log, never inferring PASS from exit code alone

knownErrors.symptom: OpenHuman's ordinary chat correctly attempts to read a file at the right action_dir path (visible in its own tool-call trace) but the read is blocked: 'This action is blocked by your safety settings... path is outside the allowed workspace'
knownErrors.rootCause: action_dir and actual file-read permission are two separate settings. OpenHuman's [autonomy] workspace_only=true confines file/glob/list tools to an internal workspace_dir regardless of what action_dir points at (action_dir is 'the acting-tool CWD', workspace_dir is a separate 'internal state, agent-blocked' root per OpenHuman's own RPC schema). Setting action_dir alone is necessary but not sufficient for the agent to actually read files there.
protection: to grant real read (or read/write) access to a directory outside the workspace while leaving workspace_only=true and everything else locked down, add an entry to [autonomy] trusted_roots: { path = "...", access = "read" } — the official mechanism per config_update_autonomy_settings' own RPC schema description
forbidden_paths entries still apply on top of trusted_roots (documented: "credential dirs stay blocked regardless") — granting a trusted_root does not bypass secret-path protection added separately

verify with a real ordinary-chat probe request in a genuinely NEW chat thread after any autonomy-settings change — an existing chat thread that already got blocked once may not retry the tool call even after the underlying config is fixed
knownErrors.solution: add the target directory to autonomy.trusted_roots with access='read' (or 'readwrite' only if genuinely needed), restart OpenHuman, and re-test in a new chat thread

knownErrors.symptom: a write to a folder granted readwrite via autonomy.trusted_roots is blocked with 'policy-blocked: Resolved parent path escapes workspace: <a DIFFERENT, unrelated read-only trusted_root path>' — the error names a path that is NOT the target folder and NOT its actual parent
knownErrors.rootCause: OpenHuman's workspace-boundary check appears to match trusted_roots by raw string prefix without a path-separator boundary check. Two trusted_roots whose absolute paths share a text prefix — e.g. 'C:\...\World_server' (read) and 'C:\...\World_server AI\SomeSubfolder' (readwrite) — collide: 'World_server AI' textually starts with 'World_server' even though it is a sibling directory, not a subdirectory (the next character is a space, not a path separator). The checker resolves the write target against the wrong (read-only) entry and blocks it.
protection: when granting a new trusted_root for OpenHuman, verify its full path does not begin with the same characters as any OTHER trusted_root path already granted, even if the two are semantically unrelated siblings (not nested) — a shared text prefix is enough to trigger this bug

confirmed fix: give any new readwrite trusted_root a name whose full path shares no character-prefix with an existing entry (e.g. use 'C:\Users\<user>\Desktop\OpenHumanReports' as a standalone top-level folder rather than nesting it under 'World_server AI', which itself shares a prefix with 'World_server')

verify a new trusted_root actually works with a real write attempt (not just assuming the config is correct) before relying on it — this bug produces a real, well-formed error, not a silent failure, so it is catchable if tested
knownErrors.solution: move the write target to a folder path with no shared text prefix against any other trusted_root, restart OpenHuman, and confirm with a real write attempt
